records.name: Ardella's House
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps women and girls with criminal justice histories find work, housing, and health care, and rebuild family life. It runs housing for women coming home from incarceration, job training, mentoring, and reentry classes.
records.what_you_do: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Survey to offer time, or ask for a guest speaker for your group. Women who want housing ask for the application packet by phone or email, then send a questionnaire and a short letter and complete a virtual interview.

cost.text: The site does not list any fees for volunteering, guest speakers or housing.

first_step.how: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Survey linked on the site, or call 267-249-3642 to ask how you can help.
first_step.basis: The volunteer survey is public and easy to find, but the site does not say what happens after you send it. The housing route is longer: a questionnaire, a letter and a required virtual interview.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a volunteer shift or how long a visit takes. Housing works as an application, not a walk in: you request the packet, send it back, and complete a virtual interview before any acceptance. Staff review each application for fit, and accepted women may get help planning their release if they need it.
first_visit_tips: For housing, have your questionnaire and a short letter about your goals ready before you contact staff.
The site lists two phone numbers, 267-249-3642 on the contact page and 267-228-4169 for requesting housing materials. Ask which one fits your question.

records.notes: Housing eligibility from the housing page: women returning from incarceration in the Philadelphia area. No age limit, sobriety rule or required referral source is stated on that page. Two phone numbers are published: 267-249-3642 on the contact page (recorded as phone) and 267-228-4169 under Request Materials on the housing page. A reviewer should confirm which is current. The contact page email is hidden behind protected text, so no email is recorded. The Sisters Empowerment Circle is a monthly donor group, not a program for women served, so it is left out of what_you_do. The annual report link was not opened. The newcomer rating of 3 applies to volunteering; the housing route would rate lower.

records.name: Mission of Hope and Redemption
records.summary: A volunteer-run food pantry in Philadelphia where families choose their own groceries. It serves about 200 families a week and also runs outreach with essential supplies and school support.
records.what_you_do: Register in person at the Thursday pantry, then shop for your own food. Volunteers help run the pantry, and the group asks people to reach out through its contact page to join.

schedule.text: Food pantry every Thursday from 11 am to 1:30 pm.

cost.text: The site lists no fee for the pantry.

first_step.how: Go to the pantry on a Thursday between 11 am and 1:30 pm and register in person with your name, address and phone number.
first_step.basis: The pantry has a set day, hours and address, and registration happens when you arrive. The site does not list eligibility rules or a phone line.
first_step.what_to_expect: You register when you arrive, giving your name, address and phone number. Then you pick the foods that fit your household's needs, a shopping style the group calls client choice. The site does not say how long a visit takes, whether bags are given, or what else happens there.
first_visit_tips: Have your name, address and phone number ready for registration.
Bring your own bags, since the site does not say whether bags are provided.
The site does not list eligibility, so ask at the door if you are not sure you qualify.

records.notes: Pantry day, hours and church address come from the Get Help page. The 200 families a week and 15 volunteers come from the About page, which dates neither figure. The About page gives December 2023 as the founding date; that is an origin date, not dated activity, so it did not change status. The contact page has only a Google form, so no phone or email is recorded. The events page lists three event names (a painting event and a back to school giveaway) with no dates, so none was used. The pantry is hosted in a church, and the site does not say whether that matters for who attends. Eligibility is not stated.
